ideas.idea: Offer a second pawn so your queen-side knight can develop by recapturing. White gives up a central pawn but gets a lead in development and open lines. Your job is to make those lines matter before Black builds a compact defensive position.
ideas.structure: The c- and d-files are potential routes into Black's position. Black often keeps a d6/e6 shell: sturdy, but sometimes cramped until the pieces find squares. Pawn breaks can change everything, so watch Black's freeing central advances rather than only the extra pawn.
ideas.pieces: Develop both knights, put a bishop on an active diagonal, and castle. Rooks often belong on the central open files; the queen can support them without becoming the first attacker. Coordinate the whole army before spending more material.
ideas.motifs: Pins on a central file, pressure against d6, and a knight arriving with tempo are recurring opportunities. Black also has counterplay: queen attacks on the queen-side and tactical jumps by a knight can punish loose pieces. Check your queen's safety before pursuing a tempting pawn.
ideas.declined: A knight-development decline can lead to positions resembling a c3 Sicilian, while a pawn advance asks you to use your space sensibly. In either case you may have equal material rather than a gambit attack. Take the useful centre and develop; do not sacrifice again just to recreate the accepted line.
ideas.caution: Exchanging active pieces indiscriminately can leave you simply a pawn down. Still, refusing every trade is not a plan: evaluate which pieces actually sustain your pressure.

modelGames.summary: A Morra specialist beats a much higher-rated opponent. White develops fast, sacrifices a knight on d5 to blast open the centre and never lets Black's king leave e8 safely.

moments.title: Development first
moments.note: Every white piece except the queen and rooks is out, and White has castled. Black has an extra pawn but his kingside is still at home.

moments.title: The knight jumps in
moments.note: White offers a knight on d5. Taking it opens the e-file toward Black's uncastled king—the kind of sacrifice the Morra's lead in development makes possible.

moments.title: A wedge on d6
moments.note: The pawn on d6 splits Black's position in two and smothers the dark-squared bishop. Black's pieces cannot coordinate around it.

moments.title: Open the f-file
moments.note: f4 hits the central knight-supporting pawn and opens another line toward e8. Attacks on a central king need open files more than extra pieces.

moments.title: The king is chased
moments.note: Bf7+ drives the king to d8. With the king running and the dark-squared bishop pinned, White's threats keep arriving faster than Black can parry them.

moments.title: Material back, and more
moments.note: White has recovered the gambit pawn with interest. The lead in development turned into a decisive attack before Black ever castled.

modelGames.summary: Black develops calmly, trades the attacking knights and keeps a compact position. Once White's initiative fades, the extra pawn and the half-open g-file give Black the long-term edge.

moments.title: A calm, solid setup
moments.note: Black takes the pawn and starts developing quietly with ...e6. The plan is simple: finish development, castle, and let White prove the compensation.

moments.title: Trade the attackers
moments.note: Black swaps the knight on f3, one of White's best attacking pieces. Each trade reduces the value of White's development lead.

moments.title: Queenside locked down
moments.note: With ...b6 Black secures the queenside. White's pressure on the half-open files has no clear target, and the extra pawn is still there.

moments.title: Turning the tables
moments.note: Black opens the g-file toward White's king. Once the defender is safe, the gambit pawn can become a springboard for counterplay.

moments.title: An extra centre pawn
moments.note: After ...f5 and ...fxe4 Black collects a central pawn. In the endgame, the material the gambit gave up finally tells.

moments.title: Passed pawns win
moments.note: Black's central pawns advance with rook support. The defence held, and the gambit pawn decided the ending.
